chapter_theme: Pattinathar's shrine songs for Thiruvenkadu, Thiruchengodu and Thiruvotriyur: pleas to a Lord whose will cannot be read. The poet asks for a day when 'you and I' stand as one beyond the tattvas and nada, confesses that his days have passed in eating, wearing, saying and seeing the same things, does not know whether Siva will push him back into the womb or give the feet, and asks only that at death someone put ash on him and teach him the five letters. The devotees who walk the shrine's street can do what the poet cannot: their feet on his head tear the leaf of fate.
structure_note: 304 to 307 are the Thiruvenkadu verses (the fourth marked வேறு, a different metre), 308 is a single verse on Thiruchengodu, and 309 and 310 open the Thiruvotriyur set. The refrain இறைவனே ஏகநாயகனே closes 304 and 305. Each verse ends on the shrine's name, so the shrine stands in for the Lord addressed.

304.reading: Is there a day when you and I stand as one in the space beyond the elements, the inner instruments, the senses and their five fields, the three gunas and nada itself? Ocean of the bliss of the mind's dissolving, beyond debate and the differences of sects: I know nothing at all; whatever is, is your doing, Lord, sole master.
304.nuance: The first two lines climb the tattvas in order, from the five elements through the inner instruments and the senses to the gunas and nada, and place the meeting in the வெளி beyond them all. மனோலயம், the mind's dissolving, is a yogic term for the state in which the mind ceases, and the verse makes the Lord that bliss rather than its giver. The closing surrender, யாது நின் செயலே, returns at 308 and 350.

305.reading: Whoever may stay and whoever may thrive and whoever may be kin to us, is there any direction for me but you, as your holy mind knows? You who, taking pity on one poet's fine Tamil, became his errand-boy and went about all night to turn Paravai's mind, Lord, sole master.
305.nuance: The second half recalls the story told of Sundarar: Siva went by night as a messenger to Paravai to reconcile her to him. உடலை மாற்ற reads literally as 'to change her body'; the legend makes it changing her stance or mind. The point is the Lord's willingness to be a servant for a devotee's Tamil, which the poet uses to claim him as his only refuge.

306.reading: Eating what was eaten, wearing what was worn, saying again and again what was said, seeing what was seen and hearing what was heard: so all my days have gone by. Lord of Venkadu of the festival street, where the swan sits on the opened lotus, father who dances in the hall as the gods praise, grant that this change.
306.nuance: The verse has no sin to confess; its complaint is repetition, a life that only repeats itself and so has not begun. மாறருளே is read as 'grant grace that this be changed'; it could also be the vocative 'you who grant grace', which leaves the verse a bare confession.

307.reading: Pure one, stainless form, whom the dark one of the churning and the one who abides on the flower seek daily and do not see: you who removed the fetters the king put on the hands of Sendan of Nangur, where carp leap in the field channels, show yourself before me, you who dwell in Venkadu.
307.nuance: மத்தளை இருண்டான் is obscure; I take it as Vishnu (dark, of the churning) paired with Brahma on the lotus, the usual two who fail to find Siva. The Sendan of Nangur freed from a king's handcuffs is a local legend I cannot verify; the verse uses it as precedent: the Lord who showed himself to free one devotee is asked to appear to this one.

308.reading: What the mind of the fire-bodied one who sits beside the shade of the aathi tree at Sengodu may be, I cannot tell: will it push me once more into the dyeing-pit of a mother's womb, or give the holy feet that Kannan could not see? Siva's doing cannot be known.
308.nuance: கருப்ப சாயக் குழி, the dye-pit of the womb, makes rebirth a vat one is thrown back into. The verse sets the two outcomes, another birth and the feet, as equally possible and the Lord's choice alone; Kannan who could not see the feet is Vishnu digging as the boar, the standard measure of their unreachability.

309.reading: When phlegm follows on phlegm, the eyes close, awareness fails and the body itself turns false, one thing I will ask: you who own Thiruvotriyur of the fields, put holy ash on me, make my hands worship, and teach me to recite the five letters.
309.nuance: The request is for the deathbed rites of a Saiva, ash, folded hands and the mantra, asked for as a grace the dying man cannot perform for himself. மெய்யும் பொய்யாகி plays on மெய் as body and as truth: the body becomes false at the moment it stops.

310.reading: Those who are to be burned do not know it; the Lord who once burned the three cities is the Lord of southern Otriyur with its firm great walls. See, mind: to roll about so that the golden feet of those who walk its streets touch our head is what tears the leaf of fate.
310.nuance: சுடப்படுவார் அறியார் can be the people of the three cities, who did not know they were being burned, or all mortals, who do not know they will be burned on the pyre; the pun on சுடுதல் carries both. The fate-leaf torn by the devotees' feet, not the Lord's, puts the devotees' street above the shrine's sanctum.

links.note: Both close on the same surrender: 304 ends 'I know nothing, whatever is, is your doing' (ஏதுமொன்றறியேன் யாது நின் செயலே), and 350 opens 'nothing at all is my doing; all is yours'. 304 asks for union beyond the tattvas; 350 turns the same formula to the problem of why evil has come to one who did no evil in this body.

Both ask for the state in which 'you and I' are one: Pattinathar asks for a day when நீயும் நானுமாய் stand in the space beyond nada, Arunagirinathar for the bliss in which 'you and I' become one enjoyment after deeds, malas, death and birth end. Both set this union beyond the body and its tattvas.

The Kural says nothing is stronger than fate, which arrives before any other plan. Pattinathar says rolling so that the devotees' feet touch one's head tears the leaf of fate. On the Kural's plain reading fate is unbeatable; on Pattinathar's, devotion beats it. The conflict depends on taking கிழிப்பது as cancelling fate rather than only ending its grip on the mind.

Both claim that devotion breaks the writing on the head: Tirumular says that when his heart joined the Lord's feet the Lord broke up his தலைவிதி, and Pattinathar says the devotees' feet on his head tear the விதி ஏடு. Tirumular has the Lord do it; Pattinathar gives the act to the Lord's servants.

309 asks that at death someone teach him the five letters, since he will no longer be able to recite them himself; 346 lists the five letters recited within (உள்ளே எழுத்தைந்தும் ஓதவுண்டு) among the ascetic's possessions. The deathbed request shows what the possession is for.

source_issues: Unit 308 (own id siddhar:thiruppadal-thirattu:u1) is unnumbered in the source and sits between the Thiruvenkadu set and the Thiruvotriyur set; it names Sengodu (Thiruchengodu), not either shrine.
Unit 307 (own id 0270-u1) is marked வேறு, a change of metre, and is unnumbered in the Thiruvenkadu run.
